observation_tags.label: White crust
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for white powdery film on the bare surface.

observation_tags.label: Hard sealed crust
observation_tags.how_to_check: Press heel on the dry top; it does not dent.

observation_tags.label: Thin peeling crust
observation_tags.how_to_check: Peel a thin skin off the surface with your fingers.

observation_tags.label: Dark greasy patches
observation_tags.how_to_check: Rub a patch; it feels greasy and looks darker.

observation_tags.label: Shiny bare patches
observation_tags.how_to_check: Watch sun on bare spots; they shine like glass.

observation_tags.label: Bare ground
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for wide ground with no growing plants.

observation_tags.label: Dusty powdery ground
observation_tags.how_to_check: Step down; dust puffs up around your foot.

observation_tags.label: Deep cracks
observation_tags.how_to_check: Lay a stick across a crack; it fits down deep.

observation_tags.label: Fine crack network
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for fine cracks joining like a net.

observation_tags.label: Gullies and erosion
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for channels cut by running water.

observation_tags.label: Clods brick hard
observation_tags.how_to_check: Knock a dry clod; it will not break easily.

observation_tags.label: Clods crumble easy
observation_tags.how_to_check: Press a dry clod; it breaks into crumbs.

observation_tags.label: Columnar rounded clods
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at dry clods standing as rounded columns.

observation_tags.label: Slippery soapy wet
observation_tags.how_to_check: Rub wet soil between fingers; it feels soapy.

observation_tags.label: Sticky smear wet
observation_tags.how_to_check: Squeeze wet soil; it smears and sticks.

observation_tags.label: Puddles stay long
observation_tags.how_to_check: After rain, note puddles still there a day later.

observation_tags.label: Puddles drain fast
observation_tags.how_to_check: After rain, puddles are gone within a short while.

observation_tags.label: Water runs off
observation_tags.how_to_check: Pour a bucketful; water runs off the surface.

observation_tags.label: Deep mud when wet
observation_tags.how_to_check: Walk after rain; feet sink deep into mud.

observation_tags.label: Hole water stays long
observation_tags.how_to_check: Fill a hand-dug hole; water still there next day.

observation_tags.label: Hardpan below surface
observation_tags.how_to_check: Push a pointed stick down; it stops hard.

observation_tags.label: Chalky lumps present
observation_tags.how_to_check: Dig and look for soft white lumps that crumble.

observation_tags.label: Dark soil colour
observation_tags.how_to_check: Compare dug soil with a clean cloth; it looks dark.

observation_tags.label: Grey soil colour
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at dug soil; it has a grey tinge.

observation_tags.label: Pale soil colour
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at dug soil; it is pale and washed.

observation_tags.label: No weeds
observation_tags.how_to_check: Walk the field; you find almost no weeds.

observation_tags.label: Salt loving weeds
observation_tags.how_to_check: Note weeds growing where the white crust is.

observation_tags.label: Hardy grass weeds
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for tough grasses surviving where crops fail.

observation_tags.label: Stunted yellow plants
observation_tags.how_to_check: Compare plant height and leaf colour with healthy land.

observation_tags.label: Scorched leaf edges
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at leaf tips and edges for browning.

observation_tags.label: Few surviving trees
observation_tags.how_to_check: Compare living trees with dead standing ones.

observation_tags.label: Patches of healthy growth
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for greener patches among the poor growth.

observation_tags.label: Salty water
observation_tags.how_to_check: Taste a single drop; it tastes salty.

observation_tags.label: Soapy bitter water
observation_tags.how_to_check: Taste and smell; it is soapy or bitter.

observation_tags.label: Good water
observation_tags.how_to_check: Taste and smell; it seems clean and fresh.

observation_tags.label: Water leaves white deposit
observation_tags.how_to_check: Let a drop dry on a plate; white film remains.

observation_tags.label: Rain is only water
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask and look; the only water is rainfall.

observation_tags.label: Well available
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for a working well within easy reach.

observation_tags.label: Canal available
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for a canal or channel that can reach the land.

observation_tags.label: Pond nearby
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for a pond you can carry water from.

observation_tags.label: Water scarce in dry months
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask how water holds up in the dry weeks.

observation_tags.label: Only rough tools
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the tools on hand; they are crude.

observation_tags.label: Good tools
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the tools; they are sound and useful.

observation_tags.label: Few helpers
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask who can help; only a pair of hands.

observation_tags.label: Many helpers
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask who can help; a whole group is ready.

observation_tags.label: No seed
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look in the store; no seed grain is kept.

observation_tags.label: Some seed
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look in the store; some seed grain is kept.

observation_tags.label: No compost
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for a compost heap; none is found.

observation_tags.label: Compost available
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for a rotted heap ready to spread.

observation_tags.label: Dung available
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for animal dung you can collect.

observation_tags.label: Gypsum available
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask the market for land plaster; it can be bought.

observation_tags.label: No gypsum
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask the market; land plaster is not to be had.

observation_tags.label: Very little money
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask what can be bought; very little is possible.

observation_tags.label: Some money
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask what can be bought; a little is possible.

observation_tags.label: Rainy season
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at sky and ground; rains are falling.

observation_tags.label: Cool season
observation_tags.how_to_check: Feel the air; days and nights are cool.

observation_tags.label: Hot season
observation_tags.how_to_check: Feel the air; the days are very hot.

observation_tags.label: Heavy rain expected
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask older folk; heavy rains are expected.

observation_tags.label: Poor rain expected
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask older folk; poor rains are expected.

observation_tags.label: Goal food
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask the person; their aim is food.

observation_tags.label: Goal cash
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask the person; their aim is money.

observation_tags.label: Goal fodder
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask the person; their aim is animal feed.

observation_tags.label: Goal long term trees
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask the person; their aim is trees over years.

observation_tags.label: Flat land
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look across the field; it lies level.

observation_tags.label: Sloping land
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look across the field; it tilts downward.

observation_tags.label: Low spot collects water
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the lowest spot after rain; water sits.

observation_tags.label: Large land
observation_tags.how_to_check: Pace the field; it takes many paces across.

observation_tags.label: Small land
observation_tags.how_to_check: Pace the field; it takes only a few paces.

observation_tags.label: Market near
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask how long the trip to market takes.

observation_tags.label: Market far
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask how long the trip to market takes.

observation_tags.label: Previously farmed
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask older folk; the land was farmed before.

observation_tags.label: Never farmed bare
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask older folk; the land was never cropped.

observation_tags.label: Overgrazed
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look for cropped grass and many hoof marks.

observation_tags.label: Previously flooded
observation_tags.how_to_check: Ask older folk; flood water covered the land.

observation_tags.label: Photo white crust
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the photo for a white powdery top.

observation_tags.label: Photo cracked surface
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the photo for cracked dry ground.

observation_tags.label: Photo standing water
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the photo for water lying on top.

observation_tags.label: Photo bare ground
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the photo for ground with no plants.

observation_tags.label: Photo stunted crop
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the photo for short yellow plants.

observation_tags.label: Photo gully erosion
observation_tags.how_to_check: Look at the photo for channels cut by water.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: A field with a white powdery film over the top.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: White crust means salt as well as sodium.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Dry ground split into a pattern of cracks.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Check crack depth with a stick laid across.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Water lying on the surface in a flat patch.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: See whether it sits in a low spot.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Wide ground with little or nothing growing.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Look for a few tough weeds at the edges.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Short, yellow plants standing in poor rows.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Compare leaf tips for browning and scorch.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Channels cut through the soil by running water.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Trace where the water enters and leaves.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Dark greasy looking patches on the bare soil.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Dark greasy patches mean very strong sodium.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Green patches beside bare and shiny ground.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Note which side of the ridge grows best.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: A wet surface that looks shiny and sticky.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Never till or walk this soil while wet.

photo_clue_guide.what_photo_shows: Dry clods standing as rounded columns with cracks.
photo_clue_guide.look_closer_for: Check whether the clods break with a knock.

severity_levels.how_it_looks: Thin patchy crust, some bare ground, weak stunted plants.
severity_levels.acts_when_wet: Sticky and slippery in small spots, water sinks slowly.
severity_levels.acts_when_dry: Top crusts lightly, clods break with a knock.
severity_levels.first_season_aim: Open the surface and get living roots in.

severity_levels.how_it_looks: Wide white and dark patches, hard crust over much ground.
severity_levels.acts_when_wet: Puddles stand, soil feels soapy and smears, feet sink.
severity_levels.acts_when_dry: Hard sealed crust, deep cracks, brick hard clods.
severity_levels.first_season_aim: Drainage furrows, gypsum and a tolerant cover.

severity_levels.how_it_looks: Thick white crust, greasy dark patches, land mostly bare.
severity_levels.acts_when_wet: Water runs off or stands for days, deep clinging mud.
severity_levels.acts_when_dry: Brick hard columns, wide cracks, hardpan below.
severity_levels.first_season_aim: Open surface, safe drainage, living roots only.

field_tests.name: Water ponding hole test
steps: Dig a hole a hand's depth wide and deep near the middle.
Fill it with water and note the time by sun or shade.
Check after a night and again after the next day.
Repeat in a bare patch and near any plants.

results.see: hole still full after a night
results.meaning: water will not sink, drainage is poor

results.see: hole empty within a short while
results.meaning: water sinks here, this spot drains well

results.see: water drains only at the hole edges
results.meaning: sealed surface with slow entry at the sides

field_tests.name: Dry clod test
steps: Pick a clod from a dry patch.
Press it with the heel or knock it on a stone.
Note how it breaks apart.
Look at the shape of the broken pieces.

results.see: clod will not break and rings hard
results.meaning: heavy clay soil that needs careful handling

results.see: clod breaks into crumbs easily
results.meaning: soil is workable when dry, add gypsum

results.see: clod stands as a rounded column
results.meaning: strong sodium in the clay

field_tests.name: Jar test
steps: Half fill the jar with water.
Add a few handfuls of soil and shake hard.
Set it down and watch how it settles.
Look at the layers and how long it stays cloudy.

results.see: water stays cloudy for a long time
results.meaning: much fine clay is held in the soil

results.see: grit settles at the bottom first
results.meaning: some sandy material is present

results.see: a firm layer forms at the bottom
results.meaning: a hard layer may lie below the surface

field_tests.name: Wet feel and smear test
steps: Take soil from just under the surface.
Rub it between your fingers and thumb.
Press a smear onto your palm.
Note how it feels and holds shape.

results.see: feels soapy and slick
results.meaning: sodium in the clay makes it slick

results.see: sticks and smears on the hand
results.meaning: heavy clay that clings when wet

results.see: gritty feel between the fingers
results.meaning: some sand is mixed in the clay

field_tests.name: Crust and crack look
steps: Walk the field and look at the bare surface.
Note white powder, dark greasy spots or shine.
Lay a stick across cracks to judge their depth.
Peel any thin skin of crust with your fingers.

results.see: white powder lying on the surface
results.meaning: salt comes up together with the sodium

results.see: dark greasy patches on bare soil
results.meaning: very strong sodium in these spots

results.see: dry ground cracked in a fine net
results.meaning: clay swells and shrinks, surface sealed

results.see: crust peels off as a thin skin
results.meaning: surface crusting, needs organic matter

field_tests.name: Long stick push test for hardpan
household_items: a long pointed stick or bar
steps: Choose a day when the top soil crumbles.
Push the pointed stick straight down.
Note where it stops and how hard it resists.
Try again in several bare spots.

results.see: stick stops on a hard layer
results.meaning: hardpan lies below the surface

results.see: soft white lumps come up
results.meaning: chalky material is mixed in the soil

results.see: stick goes down without much push
results.meaning: no hardpan here, soil is loose below

field_tests.name: Water taste and soap lather test
steps: Taste a drop of the water and note it.
Rub wet soap in a little of the water.
See whether lather forms or fails.
Let a drop dry on the plate.

results.see: water tastes salty
results.meaning: never use this water to wash the soil

results.see: soap will not lather and taste is bitter
results.meaning: bad water, never wash land with it

results.see: a white film is left when dry
results.meaning: salts are held in the water

results.see: good taste and good lather
results.meaning: safe for flushing the sodium downward

field_tests.name: Weed and colour clues
steps: Walk the field and note any plants.
Look which weeds grow on white or bare spots.
Dig a little soil and rub it on the cloth.
Compare the colour with the surrounding ground.

results.see: weeds grow only on white patches
results.meaning: strong salt and sodium there

results.see: tough grasses survive where crops fail
results.meaning: hardy plants suit the first season

results.see: soil on the cloth looks dark
results.meaning: very strong sodium, greasy soil

results.see: soil on the cloth looks pale and washed
results.meaning: washed pale soil, low in humus

results.see: almost no plants at all
results.meaning: nothing grows yet, start with a cover

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Top crusts lightly, yet soil still crumbles and takes water.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Break a dry clod with your heel.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: White crust and hard clods, water stands and roots tire.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Rub a wet handful; does it feel soapy.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Greasy dark patches, column clods, almost nothing grows.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Fill a hole and look again the next day.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Salt lies on top, yet the soil crumbles and drains.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Taste a drop of field water, not the crust.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Salt crust over sealed clay, water both sits and spoils.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Watch whether water leaves a film when dry.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Bare and firm, yet it drains and crumbles without salt.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Push a pointed stick down; it sinks without hard stops.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Sealed top plus a hard layer below the roots.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Push a long stick down until it stops.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Soft white lumps sit with the salt in the soil.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Dig a handspan and crumble the lumps.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Water cannot leave, so roots drown in sealed clay.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Watch whether a hole empties by the next day.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Water runs off and cuts channels through bare clay.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Follow the channels to see where water leaves.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Hooves sealed the surface and nothing holds the soil.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Look for many hoof marks on the bare ground.

diagnosis_rules.diagnosis: Land spoiled by bad well water
diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Soapy bitter water was used and crust followed after.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Rub soap in the water; lather fails to form.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Top has capped and dusts, sodium is beginning to build.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Pour a bucketful and watch whether it soaks in.

diagnosis_rules.plain_explanation: Too few signs to judge the land safely.
diagnosis_rules.tie_break_test: Run the clod test and the ponding hole test.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Nowhere for wash water to leave the land.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Gypsum cannot work and salts stay near the roots.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: A capped top that water cannot pass.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Water runs off and roots starve of air.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Loose crumbly soil near the surface.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Seeds cannot enter and roots cannot spread.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: A broken layer beneath the root zone.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Water and roots both stop at that layer.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Nothing rotted to open the clay.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Clay stays sealed and crusts after every rain.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: No land plaster to push sodium out.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Sodium keeps holding the clay closed.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Little or no good water for washing.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Sodium cannot be flushed below the roots.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Water that will not add more salt.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Washing with bad water makes the crust worse.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Bare ground with no living roots.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Rain hits hard, crust rebuilds and soil washes.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Nothing holding the soil on the slope.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Good topsoil leaves with every heavy rain.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: A dip that keeps standing water.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Standing water seals the clay deeper down.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Nothing lying on the bare surface.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Sun bakes the top and dust blows away.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Not enough hands for big work.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Big jobs must split into short easy spells.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Nothing at hand for the first sowing.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Living roots are the first aim of the season.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: Little to spend at the market.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Work must lean on dung, mulch and saved seed.

gap_rules.what_land_lacks: No tool that can break hard ground.
gap_rules.why_it_matters: Deep work must wait for soft dry days.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Good water allows a safe wash cycle.
scenario_variations.adapt: Run the wash when the canal or pond gives water.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: That well would add salt and soap to the land.
scenario_variations.adapt: Never wash with it; catch rain and seek good water.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Every fall must be caught and held.
scenario_variations.adapt: Dig catch pits and bunds before the rains arrive.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Washing must stop through the dry weeks.
scenario_variations.adapt: Keep water for plants and wash only at rainy start.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Flat land holds water unless an outlet is cut.
scenario_variations.adapt: Dig a drain furrow toward a low edge.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Runoff gives a natural way out, yet soil washes.
scenario_variations.adapt: Guide the drain safely and guard the slope.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Water and roots stop on the hard layer.
scenario_variations.adapt: Break it only when crumbly, in vertical lines.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: No hard layer below, normal loosening will do.
scenario_variations.adapt: Loosen gently and keep organic matter coming.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Soft white lumps need care during washing.
scenario_variations.adapt: Clear lumps while loosening, then dust gypsum thinly.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Salt sits with the sodium and must be flushed.
scenario_variations.adapt: Dust gypsum, then wash downward with good water.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: No visible salt, yet the clay is still sealed.
scenario_variations.adapt: Open the surface with mulch, compost and careful loosening.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Heavy rain helps washing yet cuts channels.
scenario_variations.adapt: Guard against erosion and keep drain furrows clear.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Little rain means little free washing water.
scenario_variations.adapt: Store every bucket and skip deep washing this season.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Rain loosens the land and carries sodium down.
scenario_variations.adapt: Set gypsum and cover before the rains firm the soil.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Cool dry days suit careful loosening work.
scenario_variations.adapt: Work the crust only while it crumbles in hand.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Heat caps the top and dries water fast.
scenario_variations.adapt: Mulch heavily and water only in the early morning.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Little to buy, dig with or sow.
scenario_variations.adapt: Lean on dung, mulch, saved seed and cover plants.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Work can move faster with bought supplies.
scenario_variations.adapt: Buy land plaster and seed, yet avoid market nitrogen alone.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Only a pair of hands at any time.
scenario_variations.adapt: Split work into short easy spells across many days.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: A group can finish big jobs together.
scenario_variations.adapt: Organise a shared day for furrows and bunds.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Food must come from tolerant crops first.
scenario_variations.adapt: Sow rice, barley or sorghum on ridge sides.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Cash crops fail on sealed clay at first.
scenario_variations.adapt: Begin with forage grass, then cash crops after improvement.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Fodder grasses tolerate salt and hold the soil.
scenario_variations.adapt: Sow karnal grass, rhodes grass and dhaincha together.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Trees give roots and shade over many seasons.
scenario_variations.adapt: Plant neem and pongamia; warn that prosopis spreads.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Small land can be finished in short spells.
scenario_variations.adapt: Work one corner first, then move along the field.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Wide land must be split into sections.
scenario_variations.adapt: Take one strip at a time through the season.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Runoff crosses the land and cuts channels.
scenario_variations.adapt: Build contour bunds and stop grazing above.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: The dip gathers water and seals the clay.
scenario_variations.adapt: Raise beds and lead water out of the dip.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Untouched land has never been worked or drained.
scenario_variations.adapt: Start slow; open the surface before any sowing.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Old farmland may still hold furrows and roots.
scenario_variations.adapt: Reuse old bunds and add gypsum with compost.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Hooves sealed the surface and removed cover.
scenario_variations.adapt: Stop grazing first, then mulch and reseed with cover.

scenario_variations.effect_on_plan: Flood water left salt and silt on top.
scenario_variations.adapt: Look for white crust and flush with good rainwater.

water_guidance.advice: Taste one drop; salty water must never wash this land.
Rub soap in the water; failed lather means keep it away.
Mix doubtful water with good water only while lather still forms.
Let a bucket stand until grit sinks, then pour off clear water.
Catch every fall in pits and pots; rainwater suits washing best.
Dust gypsum, then wash a little at a time through the season.
Never wash without an outlet, nor with salty or soapy water.
Hold water for plants only; put washing off until the rains.
Keep pond edges bunded and draw small bucketfuls so it lasts.
Stop washing with that well; turn to rain and good water.

questions_to_ask_survivor.question: After rain, do puddles stand, and do they dry within a short while?
Does a hand-dug hole still hold water the next day?
Is there white powder lying on the bare surface?
Are there dark greasy patches that look wet even when dry?
Do dry lumps break easily, or ring hard like a brick?
Does wet soil feel soapy or smear across your hand?
Are there deep cracks or soft white lumps when you dig?
How does your water taste, and does soap make lather?
Does a drop of water leave a white film when dry?
Where does your water come from through the dry weeks?
Do channels cut through the land where water runs off?
What grows unplanted — tough grass, salt weeds, or nothing?
Do the plants stand short and yellow with burnt leaf edges?
Is the land flat, sloping, or does a low spot hold water?
How many hands can help, and what tools are on hand?

everyday_measures.how_to_use: A closed hand can hold this much seed or dung.
Both hands cupped together carry this to the spot.
A full bucket spreads water or thin compost.
A full woven basket carries weeds, mulch or dung.
A full cloth sack buys or stores plaster and seed.
One ordinary step; pace the field to judge its size.
One big step; space rows and ridges by this.
Spread thumb to little finger; space plants and widths.
One finger laid sideways; a fine sowing depth.
Push the thumb in; a shallow seed depth.
Soil up to the first knuckle; a grain seed depth.

fix_protocol.title: Stop grazing and protect the land
fix_protocol.do: Keep animals off and fence the bare or broken spots.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a low brush fence around each damaged patch
fix_protocol.how: Pile cut brush or thorn in a low ring to keep cattle out.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Do this before any other work, in any season.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Thorny branches and a watchful neighbour cost nothing.
fix_protocol.caution: Do not lock away all grazing; leave the herd another patch.
fix_protocol.why: Cattle seal the surface and eat the cover that holds soil.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: You see new shoots where the ground was bare.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not let animals back until plants stand a handspan tall.

fix_protocol.title: Slow and catch running water
fix_protocol.do: Cut small cross bunds and fill gullies with brush and stone.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a bund every few paces down the slope
fix_protocol.how: Pile soil, brush and stone across the gully to slow water.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Do this before the heavy rains are expected.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Stones, brush, old baskets and earth make good barriers.
fix_protocol.caution: Never dam a gully so strongly that water breaks through.
fix_protocol.why: Slowing water keeps the good topsoil on the land.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: After rain the water runs clear, not muddy.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not leave a gully open through the rainy season.

fix_protocol.title: Cut drain furrows with an outlet
fix_protocol.do: Cut shallow furrows that lead water off to a safe outlet.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: furrows about a pace apart, a hand's depth deep
fix_protocol.how: Open furrows down the slope to a ditch or dry channel.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Cut them before the rains, while soil is dry enough.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: A hoe and a strong back are enough.
fix_protocol.caution: Never cut furrows while the soil is wet and slippery.
fix_protocol.why: Water must leave the field or sodium cannot wash down.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: A test bucketful runs away through the furrows.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not let furrow water stand in the low corner.

fix_protocol.title: Plant on raised ridges and beds
fix_protocol.do: Raise beds and sow on the side of the ridge, never the crest.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: ridges a handspan tall and a long stride apart
fix_protocol.how: Pull soil into low ridges and set seed on the sloping side.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Make ridges when the soil is dry enough to crumble.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: A hoe, a basket and steady work raise good beds.
fix_protocol.caution: On the crest seedlings dry; in the furrow they drown.
fix_protocol.why: Ridge sides give air to roots and let water pass.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: Plants on the ridge side stand greener than the furrow.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not plant in the furrow bottom or on the dry crest.

fix_protocol.title: Keep water from ponding
fix_protocol.do: Fill the low spot a little and lead standing water away.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a basketful of soil moved from each high edge
fix_protocol.how: Spread soil over the dip and open a shallow channel outward.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Do this before the rains so the dip never fills.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Any spare soil and brushwood will do.
fix_protocol.caution: Do not bury good topsoil in the dip; keep it for beds.
fix_protocol.why: Standing water seals the clay and kills the roots below.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: The dip dries soon after rain, leaving no puddle.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not leave a bowl shape that holds water for days.

fix_protocol.title: Break the hard surface crust
fix_protocol.do: Scratch and lift the sealed crust so water can enter.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: break the whole crust about a finger width deep
fix_protocol.how: Rake or hoe lightly, then drag a thorny branch over the top.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Work only when the crust is dry and lifts in flakes.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: A thorny branch or a rough harrow does the job.
fix_protocol.caution: Never break crust when it is wet and sticky.
fix_protocol.why: An open surface lets rain in and air reach the roots.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: A poured bucketful sinks quickly into the broken top.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not turn the crust deep or bring up salty subsoil.

fix_protocol.title: Loosen the top when it crumbles
fix_protocol.do: Loosen the top hand's depth only when dry crumbs form.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: one hand's depth, and no deeper
fix_protocol.how: Lift the soil with a hoe and break clods as they fall.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Start when a clod crumbles in the hand, not before.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: A hoe and patience loosen as well as any ox.
fix_protocol.caution: Wet working smears the clay and seals it worse.
fix_protocol.why: Loose dry soil takes water, air and roots easily.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: A dropped clod breaks into crumbs, not bricks.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not dig or drive animals over ground when wet.

fix_protocol.title: Break hardpan with a long bar
fix_protocol.do: Drive a long pointed bar down in lines to crack the hardpan.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: lines a long stride apart, many holes each
fix_protocol.how: Push the bar down vertically in a line, then repeat beside it.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Only when the deep soil is dry enough to shatter.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: A long pointed stick or iron bar works; no machine needed.
fix_protocol.caution: Never force the bar in wet soil; it will only smear.
fix_protocol.why: Broken hardpan lets water and roots reach below.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: The bar sinks a hand's depth more than before.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not dig a pit; break it in lines, not heaps.

fix_protocol.title: Dust the land with gypsum
fix_protocol.do: Spread land plaster thin and mix it into the crumbly top.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a handful to each basketful of soil, spread thin
fix_protocol.how: Scatter gypsum, then mix it into the top hand's depth.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Dust it when the soil crumbles and rain is coming.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: If plaster is scarce, use dung and green manure first.
fix_protocol.caution: Never mix gypsum into wet, smeared clay.
fix_protocol.why: Calcium in the plaster pushes the sodium out of the clay.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: Water sinks faster and the white crust fades.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not use wood ash or quicklime in its place.

fix_protocol.title: Add compost and dung
fix_protocol.do: Spread well-rotted compost or dung over the surface.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a basketful to every few paces of ground
fix_protocol.how: Spread it even, then mix it lightly into the top hand's depth.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Apply before the rains, on soil dry enough to crumble.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: A household rotted heap and cattle dung cost nothing.
fix_protocol.why: Rotted matter opens the clay and cuts the crust.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: The top stays crumbly after the next rain.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not spread fresh dung thick or trust market nitrogen alone.

fix_protocol.title: Catch and store rainwater
fix_protocol.do: Catch roof and surface water in pits, pots and small bunds.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a pit a few paces across and a hand's depth deep
fix_protocol.how: Dig catch pits by the paths and bund the edges to hold water.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Prepare the pits before the rain signs appear.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Old pots, pits and earth bunds catch water cheaply.
fix_protocol.caution: Keep animals and dirty runoff out of drinking stores.
fix_protocol.why: Rainwater is the best water for washing sodium away.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: The pits still hold water into the dry weeks.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not let stored water grow stale or fill with silt.

fix_protocol.title: Wash the sodium down with good water
fix_protocol.do: Wash gypsum into the soil with good water that can drain.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a bucketful at a time, letting each soak in
fix_protocol.how: Pour slowly, let it sink, and let the furrow carry water out.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Wash after dusting gypsum, as the rains begin.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Rain caught in pits washes as well as canal water.
fix_protocol.caution: Never wash with salty or soapy water, nor without an outlet.
fix_protocol.why: The wash carries the freed sodium below the root zone.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: Water sinks steadily and the crust weakens.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not flood the whole field at once without a drain.

fix_protocol.title: Grow a green manure and mix it in
fix_protocol.do: Sow a quick cover and mix its growth into the topsoil.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: seed scattered a finger width apart across the strip
fix_protocol.how: Broadcast dhaincha or a cover, then cut and mix it in.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Sow at rainy start; mix it in while still soft.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Saved dhaincha seed and a hoe are enough.
fix_protocol.caution: Do not let the cover grow woody or go to seed.
fix_protocol.why: Green matter opens clay, feeds soil life and shades the top.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: The buried cover rots into dark crumbly soil.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not plough the cover deep while ground is wet.

fix_protocol.title: Cover the bare surface with mulch
fix_protocol.do: Lay cut grass, straw or leaves over the bare ground.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: a loose layer about a thumb depth thick
fix_protocol.how: Spread mulch between plants and over bare patches, off the stems.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Mulch after the first good rain while soil holds damp.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Crop waste, dry grass and leaves are free mulch.
fix_protocol.caution: Keep mulch off wet smeared clay until it dries.
fix_protocol.why: Mulch stops baking, crusting and dust blowing away.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: The soil under the mulch stays damp and crumbly.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not heap mulch on stems or leave ground bare.

fix_protocol.title: Sow tolerant cover and first crops
fix_protocol.do: Sow salt-tolerant crops first and keep living roots in the soil.
fix_protocol.amount_everyday: seed set a finger width deep on the ridge side
fix_protocol.how: Sow barley, sorghum, cotton, dhaincha or grass on ridge sides.
fix_protocol.timing_signs: Sow at rainy start, on ridge sides, in dry crumbly soil.
fix_protocol.cheap_alternative: Dhaincha, barley and saved seed cost little.
fix_protocol.caution: Pulses, vegetables, groundnut and maize fail until land improves.
fix_protocol.why: Living roots hold the soil, shade it and feed soil life.
fix_protocol.checkpoint_sign: Plants grow evenly and green even after rain.
fix_protocol.what_not_to_do: Do not sow a sensitive crop on sealed clay or in furrows.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Walk the protected patch and look at the ground.
verification_checks.good_sign: Young shoots or weeds stand where it was bare.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Fresh hoof marks and cropped ground still show.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Mend the brush fence and warn the herders again.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Look at the gullies and cross bunds after rain.
verification_checks.good_sign: Water leaves clear and the bunds still stand.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Bunds broken and muddy water cutting a new channel.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Rebuild the bunds with more stone and brush.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Pour a bucketful into a furrow and follow it.
verification_checks.good_sign: Water flows away and the furrow bed stays open.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Water stands in the furrow or backs into the field.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Clear the outlet and deepen the furrow a little.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Feel the ridge side and look at the sown plants.
verification_checks.good_sign: Ridge sides are firm and the plants stand green.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Ridges washed flat or plants rotting in the furrow.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Raise the ridges again and set the plants higher.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Look at the low spot after a heavy rain.
verification_checks.good_sign: The dip drains soon and no puddle stays.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Water still lies in the dip for days.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Open the outlet wider and add more soil to the dip.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Pour a bucketful slowly on the broken top.
verification_checks.good_sign: Water sinks in without running off.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Water still pools and runs away over the surface.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Rake the crust again and add compost to the top.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Pick up a clod and crumble it in the hand.
verification_checks.good_sign: It breaks into fine crumbs with light pressure.
verification_checks.bad_sign: It stays a hard brick or smears when squeezed.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Stop work, wait for drier soil, then loosen again.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Push the long bar down where you broke the pan.
verification_checks.good_sign: The bar sinks a hand's depth deeper than before.
verification_checks.bad_sign: The bar still stops short on solid hardpan.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Run more lines when the deep soil is dry.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Look at the white crust and pour a bucketful.
verification_checks.good_sign: Crust fades and water sinks into the treated strip.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Crust returns thick and water still stands.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Dust again thin and wash with good water.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Feel the topsoil after the next rain.
verification_checks.good_sign: The top stays crumbly and dark, not sealed.
verification_checks.bad_sign: A hard cap forms again over the spread ground.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Add more rotted matter and mulch the surface.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Lift the lid and look into the water pit.
verification_checks.good_sign: The pit still holds clean water in dry weeks.
verification_checks.bad_sign: The pit is dry, cracked or full of silt.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Clear the silt and line the pit with clay.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Taste the wash water and watch it sink.
verification_checks.good_sign: Water tastes good, lathers, and sinks steadily.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Water tastes salty or soapy and the top seals.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Stop washing, find good water or wait for rain.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Dig a little where the cover was mixed in.
verification_checks.good_sign: Rotted green matter has made dark crumbs.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Cover lies unrotted and woody, or ground shows bare.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Chop it smaller, mix it in and keep the top damp.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Lift the mulch and feel the soil under it.
verification_checks.good_sign: Soil beneath is damp and crumbly to the hand.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Bare ground shows and the top is baked hard.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Spread more mulch over the bare patches.

verification_checks.check_by_hand_or_eye: Look along the rows and feel the soil between.
verification_checks.good_sign: Plants grow green and the soil between stays open.
verification_checks.bad_sign: Plants yellow or die and the ground seals again.
verification_checks.if_bad_do: Resow with a hardier cover and keep the ridge sides.

what_if.situation: No gypsum can be found.
what_if.do: Use dung, compost and green manure first, then wash with rainwater.

what_if.situation: No good water is at hand.
what_if.do: Catch rainwater and put washing off until the rains.

what_if.situation: Heavy rain falls and water races.
what_if.do: Open drains, guard gullies and keep animals off wet soil.

what_if.situation: The rains fail and the soil stays dry.
what_if.do: Mulch hard, protect the cover and hold every drop.

what_if.situation: Pests and disease appear on the crop.
what_if.do: Hand-pick, keep plants strong and remove weak diseased ones.

what_if.situation: Money is very short for the market.
what_if.do: Lean on dung, mulch, saved seed and neighbourly help.

what_if.situation: Too few hands for the work.
what_if.do: Split jobs into short spells and do the smallest useful thing.

what_if.situation: Only rough tools are on hand.
what_if.do: Work when soil crumbles and use a pointed stick well.

what_if.situation: A hard layer is found below.
what_if.do: Break it in dry weather with a long bar in lines.

what_if.situation: Water ponds after rain.
what_if.do: Lead the water out and fill the dip a little.

what_if.situation: Good seed is scarce.
what_if.do: Sow dhaincha, barley or grass and save seed from them.

what_if.situation: The market price is low.
what_if.do: Grow food and fodder first and sell only the surplus.

what_if.situation: The soil seems to get worse.
what_if.do: Stop heavy work, keep the surface open, add organic matter.

what_if.situation: Young plants fail early.
what_if.do: Check for crust, salt and standing water, then resow hardy cover.

what_if.situation: The soil shows signs of improving.
what_if.do: Keep cover, add organic matter and widen the tolerant crops.

what_if.situation: The white crust returns after washing.
what_if.do: Dust gypsum again thin and wash with good water only.

what_if.situation: Rain comes too early.
what_if.do: Sow the cover quickly and guard bare ground from washing.

what_if.situation: Rain comes too late.
what_if.do: Hold the seed, mulch the surface and wash nothing yet.

what_if.situation: Animals enter the field.
what_if.do: Mend the fence and lead the herd to a grazing patch.

what_if.situation: Wind blows dust off the field.
what_if.do: Mulch the bare top and leave rough clods on the surface.

what_if.situation: Flood water comes from upslope.
what_if.do: Cut a diversion bund to turn the water aside.

what_if.situation: Only salty water is available.
what_if.do: Never wash with it; save it for nothing but the roadside.

what_if.situation: Gypsum is too costly or hard to get.
what_if.do: Improve with dung and green manure, and wash in the rains.

what_if.situation: No way for water to leave can be found.
what_if.do: Make raised beds, catch rain and wash only small amounts.

not_in_kb_message: I have no note on that yet; gather more clues and I will try again.
advisor_rules: Never ask for or quote readings or numbers; use eyes, hands and household items.
Always give a hands-and-eyes check the survivor can do alone.
Give amounts in everyday terms: a handful, a bucketful, a pace.
Always say why, so the survivor understands the land.
Explain why sensitive crops fail until the land improves.
Always offer one clear next step to try now.
Admit gaps plainly instead of guessing.
Stay cautious and hedge when clues are missing.

diseases.name: Leaf spot
diseases.how_to_spot: Brown or dark spots spread over the leaves.
diseases.cause: Damp crowded leaves with little air between plants.
diseases.home_cure: Spray a neem leaf soak and remove the worst leaves.
diseases.prevention: Space plants well, weed, and open drainage for air.
diseases.stage_when_seen: In the damp growing weeks before flowering.

diseases.name: Rust
diseases.how_to_spot: Red-brown dusting powder on leaves and stems.
diseases.cause: Damp warm weather with crowded plants.
diseases.home_cure: Remove sick plants and spray a neem leaf soak.
diseases.prevention: Space plants, weed well and avoid overwatering.
diseases.stage_when_seen: As the crop grows tall, before grain forms.

diseases.name: Aphids
diseases.how_to_spot: Tiny clusters on soft shoots, sometimes sticky.
diseases.cause: Warm still weather with soft crowded growth.
diseases.home_cure: Wash them off with a soapy water spray and by hand.
diseases.prevention: Space plants, control weeds and encourage ladybirds.
diseases.stage_when_seen: On young shoots in warm still spells.

diseases.name: Stem borer
diseases.how_to_spot: Holes in stems, drooping heads and sawdust powder.
diseases.cause: Moths laying eggs on crowded young plants.
diseases.home_cure: Cut and remove damaged stems and hand-pick the grubs.
diseases.prevention: Space plants, keep the field clean and sow on time.
diseases.stage_when_seen: In young plants up to heading.

diseases.name: Root rot
diseases.how_to_spot: Plants wilt and roots are dark, soft and rotted.
diseases.cause: Waterlogged sealed clay with no air around roots.
diseases.home_cure: Remove sick plants and open drainage furrows at once.
diseases.prevention: Raise beds, improve drainage and never overwater.
diseases.stage_when_seen: Whenever the soil stays wet too long.

diseases.name: Blast
diseases.how_to_spot: Leaf patches grey with dark edges, poor heads.
diseases.cause: Damp crowded growth under heavy water.
diseases.home_cure: Drain the water a little and remove sick leaves.
diseases.prevention: Space clumps, keep water shallow and sow on time.
diseases.stage_when_seen: On young plants in damp standing water.

diseases.name: Wilt
diseases.how_to_spot: Plants droop and wilt even while the soil is damp.
diseases.cause: Sealed clay, salt and rotted roots cut water off.
diseases.home_cure: Remove sick plants and open drainage so roots get air.
diseases.prevention: Raise beds, add compost and plant on ridge sides.
diseases.stage_when_seen: Any time the soil stays sealed and salty.

diseases.name: Caterpillars
diseases.how_to_spot: Chewed leaves and fat grubs under the leaves.
diseases.cause: Eggs laid by moths on soft green leaves.
diseases.home_cure: Hand-pick the grubs each morning and remove them.
diseases.prevention: Space plants, keep weeds down and watch leaves closely.
diseases.stage_when_seen: While leaves are soft and green.

diseases.name: Termites
diseases.how_to_spot: Mud tubes, hollow stems and dying young trees.
diseases.cause: Dry soil with dead wood and old stumps left about.
diseases.home_cure: Dig out the nest and pour a neem leaf soak around it.
diseases.prevention: Clear dead wood, keep soil damp and mulch the base.
diseases.stage_when_seen: Mostly in the dry hot spells.

diseases.name: Damping-off
diseases.how_to_spot: Seedlings fall over with rotten thin stems at the base.
diseases.cause: Wet crowded seedbeds with little air.
diseases.home_cure: Remove sick seedlings and let the top dry a little.
diseases.prevention: Space seeds, water less and keep the bed open.
diseases.stage_when_seen: In the nursery, just after seedlings rise.

crop_selection_rules.reason: Hardy crops push through crust and open the top.
Only crops that take wet feet survive standing water.
Bad water means choose crops that need little watering.
Good water lets thirsty crops grow and land be washed.
Rain-fed crops must be hardy and safe in drought.
Deep-rooted crops reach into a broken hardpan.
A rainy start suits tolerant cover and wet crops.
Cool dry weeks suit grain and oil seed crops.
Hot weeks suit millet and drought-hardy crops.
Low-care crops need few hands and little weeding.
Simple crops do not need fine tillage or good tools.
Cheap seed and free cover suit an empty purse.
Food crops feed the family from tolerant land.
Cash crops sell, yet they need better soil first.
Forage grasses feed cattle and hold the soil.
Trees give long cover; prosopis can spread like a weed.
Deep-rooted cover holds the soil on sloping ground.
Only wet-foot crops suit a low, water-holding dip.
A near market lets cash crops be sold fresh.
Sturdy storable crops travel well to a far market.
Start with seed that is easy to find or save.
Sow saved tolerant seed first on bare land.
Improved land can carry a fussier crop again.
Severe land needs only cover, grass and trees.

multi_year_path.aim: Open the surface, drain the land and keep living roots.
